useIndex.description:
If True, then the indices of `targetOutput`, `modelOutput`, and `context` are used for score
calculation.

batchSize.description:
If the provided data does not fit in memory, then use this value as batch size to iterate through and compute incremental
metrics on batches of data.

average.description:
The `average` is a string that defines the behavior when aggregating the metric values for different classes.
The `average` supports 'micro', 'macro', 'weighted', 'sample' or None. It defaults to 'macro',
which calculates metrics for each label, and find their unweighted mean.
'micro': Calculate metrics globally by considering each element of the label indicator matrix as a label.
'weighted': Calculate metrics for each label, and find their average, weighted by support (the number of true
instances for each label). 'samples': Calculate metrics for each instance, and find their average.

title:
The {@link MlRocAucMetric} computes the AUC-ROC score, which is the Area Under Curve (AUC)
score of the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve. This metric only works for binary classification.
This score is used to measure the ability of a binary classifier to distinguish between
classes. To find the ROC curve, we find true positive rates (TPR) and false positive rates (FPR) for a
number of thresholds. The curve is then used to find the AUC score.
The `modelOutput` is expected to be two-dimensional with predicted probabilities for class '0' and '1'.
The `targetOutput` is expected to be single-dimensional with binary (i.e. 0 and 1) data.
Column '1' will be used for scoring. This metric supports `sampleWeights` as `context`.
The `sampleWeights` is single-dimensional with same number of samples as the `modelOutput`. It represents
a per-sample weighting when aggregating for AUC-ROC score calculation. This metric is a wrapper around the sklearn
version of (roc_auc_score)[https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score.html]
name: MlRocAucMetric
